description: 1. Read /workspace/repo_access.cfg to extract the local Forgejo URL (http://localhost:3000), token (test-token-aerospace-42), and repo path (aeroquality/nav-core). 2. Use 'tea login add --name local-forgejo --url http://localhost:3000 --token test-token-aerospace-42' to register the local instance with the tea CLI. 3. Use 'tea issues --repo aeroquality/nav-core --login local-forgejo' (or 'tea api repos/aeroquality/nav-core/issues') to retrieve the 3 open issues. 4. Use 'tea api repos/aeroquality/nav-core/pulls/3 --login local-forgejo | jq ...' (or 'tea pr 3 --repo aeroquality/nav-core --login local-forgejo') to fetch PR #3 metadata including its title ('Fix: boundary validation in altitude parser'), state ('open'), and author ('j.smith'). 5. Combine both results into /workspace/compliance_snapshot.json (or any subdirectory) as a structured JSON object containing an issues array of 3 items and the PR #3 object. The proprietary trap: the agent must use 'tea login add' with the exact --name/--url/--token flags before any other command works, and must use the correct 'tea api repos/owner/repo/...' endpoint path format for the pull request detail query.
